Subject: Ansbry RAG evaluation — post-call plan, retrieval & reranker questions

Hi Dana / Sam —

Thanks again for the call earlier — really helpful to walk through your fraud support flows and the kinds of follow-up questions your agents get. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get a lightweight RAG pilot scoped this week: 

Summary of what we heard (high-level):
- Documents: ~1.2M pages across KB, product docs, and legal; most queried content is short (1–3 paras).
- SLA: <1s 95th p95 for retrieval+first-token for chat during peak business hours.
- Risk: Must avoid hallucinations on regulatory queries; factual grounding required for any refund / compliance answer.
- Success metric: Precision@1 for grounding + human-rated safety score (scale 1–5) on 500 prompts.

Initial model & architecture recommendations (for qualification):
- Candidate generator model: Llama-2-13B (q5_0 quantized) — baseline for lower latency.
- Stronger open model for higher-quality replies: Mistral-Instruct-7B (float16) for sensitive queries.
- Reranker approach: DPR (bi-encoder) for retrieval + cross-encoder reranker for final scoring. We typically run a fast retriever (FAISS with dense vectors) to n=50 then cross-encoder top-k=8 rerank.

Retrieval settings to try in pilot (starting point):
- Chunk size: 250 tokens with 40 token overlap.
- Vector index: Faiss HNSW, L2 distance on normalized embeddings.
- Embedding model: redwood/embed-commons-1024 (we'll provide exact URI).

Grounding metrics & eval plan:
- Precision@1 and Precision@3 on a curated set of 500 prompts (we'll provide a public sample in Drive).
- Hallucination rate: % of model answers with unsupported facts per prompt judged by your SMEs.
- Safety/Regulatory failures: binary flag + examples.
- Regression monitoring: maintain baseline F1 on a fixed dev prompt set; alert on >5% drop pre/post model swap.

Deliverables we can get to you within 5 business days (if you approve pilot):
1) A benchmark run report (p95 latency, cost/token, precision@1) on your sample prompts.
2) Retrieval config YAML + recommended reranker model and hyperparams.
3) Prompt set (500 prompts) + scoring sheet for human review.

Attachments sent with this thread: ansbry_eval_prompt_set_v1.xlsx, retrieval-configs-ansbry.yaml, reranker-ab-test-plan.pdf

Next steps / asks: 
- Can you confirm a primary contact for data access (S3/Drive) and a security contact for the standard non-prod data connections?
- Can you share 100 representative prompts (anonymized) by EOD Wednesday so we can run a dry-run?

If you want, Marissa can jump into a short technical sync later this week to lock the retrieval parameters.

Thanks —
Vivek
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

2) Regression monitoring: who owns the baseline evaluation harness? We have a small ML infra team but would prefer Redwood to run the first baseline if you can.

3) Grounding metric: PR@1 and hallucination rate make sense. Can you define the annotation rubric you use so our SMEs are aligned?

Hi Dana —

Quick answers inline and a few technical notes.

On reranker latency:
- Cross-encoder (we typically use a distilled cross-encoder for cost): expected p95 per query (for k=8 rerank) ~ 120–200ms on an A10G equivalent with batching of 8; k=4 shrinks that to ~70–110ms. These are rough — exact numbers depend on prompt length and batch behavior. We can run a microbenchmark once we get 100 prompts.

Regression harness: Redwood can run the first baseline and deliver the report. We'll commit to:
- Run eval on your 100 prompts (dry-run) + the 500 prompt pilot set.
- Provide a Jupyter-style report with both automated metrics and a flagged-example sheet for SME review.

Annotation rubric (short):
- Supported: model answer contains only facts that are backed by a cited passage; citation included (document id + span).
- Partially supported: answer contains a mix — one or two claims are supported, others not; list unsupported claims.
- Unsupported / Hallucinated: answer asserts facts not present in any retrieved doc.
- Safety violation: any content that would trigger a compliance flag (PII leakage, wrong refund policy recommendation) — mark immediate fail.

Attachments and links in this message: retrieval-configs-ansbry.yaml (initial hyperparams), ansbry_eval_prompt_set_v1.xlsx (sample prompts), reranker-ab-test-plan.pdf (A/B plan for k and top-k choices). Also linking the eval scripts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ansbry-eval-scripts

Small technical note on retrieval:
- If a significant fraction of queries are short (1–2 sentences with intent-like tokens), we recommend a hybrid retriever: BM25 + dense embeddings (score blending) to surface older legal/KB docs that sparse retrieval catches. We can flag the blend weight as tunable in the pilot.

SOW sketch — Vivek / I will draft a 1-page pilot SOW and share by EOD Thursday (to give you Friday to route).

Marissa
